entries.drive_summary: M5Stack 360-degree servo (9 g, as in BALA-C and the Servo Kit 360): printed servo_cradle on the outside of each panel, wheel screwed to the servo's own horn; none: open-loop speed
entries.wheel_name: Printed solid wheel, horn face, 50 x 3 O-ring
notes: Speed 0.236 m/s in simulation; turns on the spot at 135.4 degrees a second.
Steepest slope climbed in simulation: 14 degrees. Highest step: 4 mm.
Wheels at the back with a ramped start is the better arrangement: it climbs steeper, and a hard start is what lifts the support.
Fit a ring, a band or a TPU tyre to a printed wheel: bare plastic slips on a smooth floor.
For wheels at the front, pin the head on facing the other way and reverse the drive.
A printed idler tip is a third support option (tip_idler_fork, idler_hub, idler_tyre_tpu).
Print the fit pieces first.
Power: BaseX needs 9 to 12 V on its jack for the motors; its own 950 mAh cell runs the logic.
Speed is open loop: there is no feedback from these drives, so equal commands do not give a straight line.

entries.stability_verdict: centre of mass inside the triangle of the two wheels and the support, 34.7 mm from the nearest edge; tips sideways at 33.2 degrees
entries.drive_summary: Yellow TT gear motor, 1:48: printed tt_cradle on the outside of each panel, wheel on the outer shaft; none: open-loop speed (an encoder version exists)
entries.wheel_name: Printed hub with TPU tyre, TT shaft bore
notes: Speed 0.615 m/s in simulation; turns on the spot at 324.1 degrees a second.
Steepest slope climbed in simulation: 16 degrees. Highest step: 10 mm.
Wheels at the back with a ramped start is the better arrangement: it climbs steeper, and a hard start is what lifts the support.
Fit a ring, a band or a TPU tyre to a printed wheel: bare plastic slips on a smooth floor.
For wheels at the front, pin the head on facing the other way and reverse the drive.
A printed idler tip is a third support option (tip_idler_fork, idler_hub, idler_tyre_tpu).
Print the fit pieces first.
Power: a 5 V source for the Pi and a separate 4.8 to 6 V pack for the wheel drives.
Speed is open loop: there is no feedback from these drives, so equal commands do not give a straight line.
